# DSH Studio v0.9.16

## New features

- Qualify Harness `0.1.7-rc.2` with plans, goals, jobs and schedules, workflows, subagents, user questions, deliverables, and Office/PDF preview surfaces.
- Migrate legacy directory-based Agent Presets into the current Profile without deleting their sources or overwriting later Profile edits.
- Register `.dshpreset` as a native desktop file type with operating-system open, single-instance handoff, and drag-and-drop import.

## Changes and security

- Install the complete integrity-locked 599-package peer graph from the official npm registry and support the current CLI and clean same-origin authentication redirects.
- Preview and verify every portable preset before mutation, then show its identity, file count, and unpacked size for explicit trust confirmation.
- Route native open events only to the foreground Studio window, reject ambiguous arguments, and redact the one-time runtime token from verification logs.

## Fixes and polish

- Collapse duplicate startup file events and consume retained offers so multiple windows cannot show duplicate trust dialogs or repeat an old import.
- Leave the current Profile unchanged when integrity validation fails, trust is declined, or import fails.

## Installation

- Upgrade in place or use the signed in-app updater. Full includes pinned offline dependencies; Lite downloads them from official sources when required.
- Native file association is installed by packaged builds. Portable Windows builds retain picker and drag-and-drop import.

## Verification

- Production build, lint, 285 frontend tests at 95.1% statement coverage, 62 packaging tests, 415 Rust tests, accessibility checks, public-contract checks, and bilingual documentation checks passed locally.
- A clean verifier installed all 599 runtime packages, authenticated a real Web Profile, validated Host Protocol 1, and required the qualified client and host capability surfaces.
- CI builds and smoke-tests Lite, Full, and portable artifacts on Linux, Windows, and macOS before publishing checksums and the signed updater manifest.
